prompt:
Finish the `texttable` crate (src/lib.rs): `Table::render` and the rest of the `Table` API must produce exactly the output described here.

1. Layout: a top border, the header line, a header separator, one line per body line, and a bottom border. Borders are `+` followed, for each column, by `width + 2` dashes and a `+`; the header separator is the same with `=` instead of `-`. Content lines are `|`, then for each column a space, the cell padded to the column width, a space and `|`. Every line, including the last, ends with `\n`.
2. Column width is the widest header or cell line in that column (after rule 7), and at least 1. Width is measured in Unicode scalar values (`char`s), not bytes: `"café"` is 4 wide.
3. Alignment: body cells follow the column's alignment. `Align::Center` puts the extra space on the right when the padding is odd. Header cells are always centered, whatever the column's alignment.
4. Default alignment: a column with no explicit `align(...)` call is right-aligned if it has at least one non-empty body cell and every non-empty body cell (after trimming per rule 6) is a number: an optional `-`, one or more ASCII digits, and optionally a `.` followed by one or more digits (`42`, `-3.50`; not `+1`, `1.`, `.5` or `1e3`). Otherwise it is left-aligned. An explicit `align` always wins.
5. Multi-line cells: a `\n` in a cell (header or body) splits it into lines. A row is as tall as its tallest cell; shorter cells get blank lines at the bottom. Each line is aligned on its own.
6. Trailing whitespace (spaces, tabs, `\r`) is removed from every cell line; leading whitespace is kept and counts toward the width. A tab anywhere else in a line is replaced by a single space.
7. `max_width(col, w)` caps the column's width at `w` (which must be at least 1; `w == 0` panics). A line longer than `w` chars is cut to its first `w - 1` chars followed by `…` (U+2026), so it is exactly `w` wide. This applies to header lines too.
8. `add_row` with fewer cells than columns pads the row with empty cells. More cells than columns returns `Err(TableError::TooManyCells { row, expected, got })`, where `row` is the 0-based index the row would have had, and the table is left unchanged (the next successful row takes that index).
9. A table with no body rows renders as top border, header line(s), and bottom border (no `=` separator).
10. `separate_rows(true)` draws a `-` border line between consecutive body rows (not after the header separator or before the bottom border).
11. `align` and `max_width` panic if `col` is out of range. `Table::new(&[])` (no columns) renders as the empty string.
12. `render` takes `&self` and can be called any number of times with the same result; rows and settings can be changed between calls.

No dependencies; `cargo test --offline` must pass.
